prefill.quotation: One of the important wetlands of the basin named as Akgol Wetland has almost lost its water surface by 96% at the same time interval, and is in danger of extinction.
prefill.comment: This is the paper's headline result: Akgöl, once one of the largest wetlands of Türkiye, lost almost all of its open water between 1987 and 2017 in the Konya Closed Basin, a semi-arid endorheic basin with heavy irrigation. The figure comes from one Landsat image per year. The replication tests whether the loss holds when every valid Landsat scene from 1984 to 2025 is used, so that the seasonal filling and drying of the wetland cannot drive the result.

prefill.aida: Akgöl wetland in the Konya Closed Basin has lost almost all of its open water since the late 1980s.

prefill.label: Akgöl wetland lost about 96% of its water surface 1987-2017, Konya Closed Basin (Musaoğlu et al. 2018)
Replication of the Akgöl water-surface loss with every valid Landsat scene 1984-2025 on HEALPix cells
prefill.scope: The claim that Akgöl wetland lost about 96% of its water surface between 1987 and 2017 (2958.4 ha to 117.2 ha). In scope: the four yearly areas the paper reports (1987, 1998, 2007, 2017), the size of the loss when all valid scenes of each year are used, whether the loss persists through 2025, and, as context, the paper's basin-wide decline of about 23.5%. Out of scope: the GIS layers on settlements and infrastructure, and the paper's statement that the decrease matches the meteorological conditions (tested separately).
prefill.methodology: All Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 scenes (Landsat 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9) over Akgöl from 1984 to 2025, read from Microsoft Planetary Computer. For each scene the green and near-infrared bands are read for the site window, cloud, shadow, snow and fill pixels are masked with QA_PIXEL, and the bands are resampled onto HEALPix cells of about 25 m (depth 18, WGS84 ellipsoid, nested) with conservative bilinear resampling before computing NDWI as in the paper. Water is NDWI above 0, with -0.1 and +0.1 as sensitivity. A scene counts when at least 95% of the site's cells are valid (451 scenes). The site outline is the JRC Global Surface Water maximum extent. For each of the paper's years the scene closest to its value and the range over all scenes are reported; for the long-term change, the median over 1984-1995 and over 2015-2025 of each year's spring (March-June) maximum. The basin figure uses JRC Global Surface Water transitions 1984-2021 over HydroBASINS basin 2040085960.
prefill.deviation: Every valid scene instead of one hand-picked image per year; a fixed NDWI threshold with sensitivity instead of a threshold chosen per image; Collection 2 surface reflectance instead of the images processed in ERDAS; HEALPix cells of about 25 m instead of 30 m pixels; the record extended to 2025. The basin-wide figure uses JRC Global Surface Water (1984-2021) over the HydroBASINS endorheic basin instead of the paper's 16 water bodies.

prefill.label: Akgöl's loss of open water reproduced with every Landsat scene 1984-2025; it has not refilled since 2000
prefill.conclusion: The paper's loss of open water at Akgöl is reproduced. Scenes close to the paper's values exist for 1987 (3007 ha against 2958.4), 2007 (9.3 against 12.7) and 2017 (94.8 against 117.2), a loss of 96.8% from 1987 to 2017 against the paper's 96%. Using every valid scene, the median spring maximum fell from 3423 ha in 1984-1995 to 299 ha in 2015-2025, a loss of 91%, and Akgöl has not filled to half its 1984-1995 level in any year since 2000. Only the paper's 1998 value (1153.9 ha) is not matched at its threshold: our valid 1998 scenes peak at 828 ha (1152 ha at NDWI > -0.1). Single images per year hide a two-fold seasonal range (3860 ha in April and 1969 ha in July 1987), but not the loss.
prefill.evidence: 451 valid Landsat scenes of Akgöl, 1984-2025, NDWI > 0 on HEALPix depth 18 (about 25 m; depth 17 under-counted small water, results/depth_sensitivity.json). Paper years, paper value / closest scene / range over scenes (ha): 1987 2958.4 / 3006.8 (9 June) / 1969-3860, 3 scenes; 1998 1153.9 / 827.7 (7 June) / 60-828, 6 scenes; 2007 12.7 / 9.3 (31 May) / 0-28, 8 scenes; 2017 117.2 / 94.8 (27 June) / 0-429, 13 scenes. Threshold sensitivity at the closest scene, NDWI -0.1 to +0.1: 1987 2612-3445 ha; 1998 686-1152 ha; 2017 81-127 ha. Median spring maximum 1984-1995 3423 ha, 2015-2025 299 ha. Years filled to half the 1984-1995 level: 100% of the 1980s, 40% of the 1990s, none since 2000. Basin, JRC Global Surface Water 1984-2021: -20.0% (paper about -23.5%), -40.4% without Tuz Gölü. Files: results/claims.json, results/fill_by_decade.csv, results/basin_jrc.json.
prefill.limitations: NDWI misses bright or turbid water in some scenes, so single scenes can read too low; the long-term figure uses yearly spring maxima for that reason. The paper's 1998 image and its per-image thresholds are unknown, which may explain the 1998 gap. Landsat 7 scenes after 2003 whose scan-line gaps cross the site fail the 95% valid-cell rule and are dropped. The basin comparison uses a different water product and basin outline from the paper. The causes of the loss (dams, drainage, irrigation, climate) are not tested here.
